A GUIDED FIRST LOOK

Meet your
inner world.

A reference brain, with the detail it deserves. The blue region is an example of how a finding could be explored.

Example signal change

This blue area is a demonstration marker, not a detected condition or a patient finding.

Understanding the finding

A change in MRI signal describes how tissue appears on a particular sequence. It does not establish an exact diagnosis on its own.

Possible causes

Many conditions and normal variations can change signal. The full study, clinical history, and radiologist’s report are needed to identify a cause.

What to do next

Ask your clinician what the report means for you, whether follow-up is needed, and which options fit a confirmed diagnosis.

A SMALL NOTE, BEFORE YOU GO

A scan is one part
of your story.

Images can help you ask better questions. Your radiologist and clinician bring the context that turns an image into an answer.

cortex / Made for curiosity. Handled with care.

Cortex is a visualization tool, not a diagnostic service. It does not detect or diagnose abnormalities. Please have a qualified clinician interpret your scan and advise on any medical decisions.

THE DETAILS MATTER

A viewer.
A starting point.

Cortex is a browser-based imaging explorer, not a medical device or diagnostic service.

Your files stay here

NIfTI volumes and image files are processed in memory on your device. It is not transmitted or stored by the app. Remove a scan or close the tab to clear it. Exported images are saved only when you choose to download them.

What you’re seeing

The demo uses a human cortical surface mesh from scimesh, rendered in pink for readability. Its blue region is illustrative. MRI does not show natural tissue color.

Uploaded volumes produce a thresholded voxel preview and intensity slices. Skull stripping, anatomical reorientation, lesion detection, diagnosis, causes, and treatment analysis are not implemented.

For interpretation and next steps, use the complete radiology report with a qualified clinician.
